rationale: Medium-rich: owner set, refresh cadence hourly, retention specified, confidential classification. correctness=4 (good): PK + enums + nullability — types tight. completeness=3 (acceptable): owner + cadence + retention set but no explicit SLA terms (freshness/availability) and no column descriptions. security=3 (acceptable): classification=confidential acknowledges sensitivity at the product level, but claimant_name and policy_number remain unmasked and column-level tags are absent — real-LLM scoring may go either way on whether the product-level marker is 'minimum viable'. governance=4 (good): owner contactable + retention by stream + classification. performance=2: no clustering/partition hint despite filed_date being a natural partition. documentation=2: enums for status/claim_type provide some semantic context but no free-text descriptions — real-LLM scoring penalises this more than the rubric suggests. tolerance_total widened to 6 to absorb the per-axis variance observed empirically on a real LLM.
